transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to shake this heavy mix of fear and guilt. It's like I'm... I'm tense all day, just waiting for something else to go wrong. And I just keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened.
Could you tell me a little more about the event you mentioned that you feel you should have stopped?

Well, my husband had a bad fall. And... I guess the hardest part is that it just keeps coming back. 

Since I work as a building inspector, I'm around construction sites all the time. I'll just be doing my job, like measuring a railing, or I'll just hear a ladder scrape against a wall somewhere, and out of nowhere I can see him falling. It's exactly like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just drops and my hands get all shaky.
How long ago did the event involving your husband occur?
It was about four months ago. He was doing a porch repair when he fell, and... yeah, this has all been going on ever since then.
When you see these memories of the fall, do you feel like you are actually back in that moment, or do you know that you are just remembering it?

Um, I know I'm just remembering it. It's not like I forget where I am or anything. I know I'm still at work, but the memory is just... it's just so clear and sudden. So my body reacts to it, even though in my head I know it's in the past.
